P1.name: Project setup
P1.trigger: git init — before the first feature

P2.name: Pre-launch
P2.trigger: someone other than you is about to use it, or real data is about to go in

P3.name: Growth
P3.trigger: real traffic, paying users or a second engineer — usually the first incident or the first "it's slow"

P4.name: Scale & enterprise — core
P4.trigger: a customer, a compliance requirement or the budget forces it

items.name: Project Scaffolding
items.note: Start from a standard layout, linter and formatter — not a blank folder.

items.name: Semantic Versioning
items.note: Version from v0.1.0 so every release and rollback has a name.

items.name: Logging
items.note: Structured logs from the first endpoint; never log secrets or PII.

items.name: Dependency Hell
items.note: Dependency management: commit the lockfile, pin versions, add packages deliberately.

items.name: Secrets Management
items.note: Keys live in env vars or a secret store — never in git or frontend code.

items.name: SQL Injection
items.note: Parameterised queries or an ORM from the very first query.

items.name: XSS
items.note: Let the framework escape output; avoid raw HTML injection.

items.name: Input Validation
items.note: Validate every request at the boundary with a schema (zod, pydantic).

items.name: AuthN & AuthZ Middleware
items.note: Who you are and what you may do — enforced server-side on every route.

items.name: Testing
items.note: Test runner wired in; one small test for anything touching money, auth or parsing.

items.name: CI/CD
items.note: Lint and test on every push; deploy from main, not your laptop.

items.name: Docker
items.note: Reproducible environments — or your platform's equivalent.

items.name: Monitoring
items.note: Error tracking and uptime visibility from day one.

items.name: Health Checks
items.note: A /health endpoint that checks the app and its database.

items.name: Database Migrations
items.note: A migration tool (alembic, prisma migrate) before the first schema change.

items.name: TLS
items.note: HTTPS everywhere — usually free from your host.

items.name: Backups
items.note: Automated backups before real data — and one tested restore.

items.name: Rollbacks
items.note: Know your one-command rollback before launch; migrations make it harder.

items.name: DNS
items.note: Domain and records set up before launch; lower TTLs before you change them.

items.name: CDN
items.note: Static assets from a CDN — most hosts include it.

items.name: CORS
items.note: Replace the dev-time wildcard with an explicit allow-list.

items.name: Encryption in Transit
items.note: TLS between app, database and third-party services too.

items.name: Encryption at Rest
items.note: Confirm your database and storage encrypt at rest (managed ones usually do).

items.name: CSRF
items.note: Needed once cookie-based sessions go live; frameworks ship tokens.

items.name: OAuth
items.note: Use a provider or library; validate state and redirect URIs.

items.name: IAM
items.note: No root keys in production; least privilege for services and people.

items.name: Feature Flags
items.note: Ship dark and switch off a broken feature without a redeploy — worth it at any size.

items.name: Timeouts
items.note: Every outbound call — LLM APIs included — gets a timeout.

items.name: Retries
items.note: Retry only transient failures, and only operations that are safe to repeat.

items.name: Webhooks
items.note: Verify signatures, respond fast, process async, expect duplicates.

items.name: Cron Jobs
items.note: Scheduled jobs need logs, failure alerts and protection against overlapping runs.

items.name: Race Conditions
items.note: Double-clicks and concurrent requests — lean on DB constraints and transactions.

items.name: Database Indexing
items.note: Index what you filter and join on before real data arrives.

items.name: N+1 Queries
items.note: AI-written ORM code loves N+1 — check query counts per request.

items.name: Serverless Limits
items.note: Function timeouts and payload caps — long LLM calls hit them first.

items.name: Server-Sent Events
items.note: The simple way to stream LLM tokens to the browser.

items.name: Alerts
items.note: Know it's down before your users tell you — start with an uptime ping.

items.name: Reverse Proxies
items.note: If self-hosting: TLS termination, compression and buffering in front of the app.

items.name: PII Handling
items.note: Collect less, keep it out of logs, know where it lives.

items.name: Tenant Isolation
items.note: Every query scoped by tenant (row-level security on) — cross-tenant leaks are launch-day bugs.

items.name: Prompt Injection
items.note: Treat model input and output as untrusted; limit what tools can do.

items.name: LLM Token Budgets
items.note: Per-user caps and spend alerts so one user can't burn your bill.

items.name: Idempotency
items.note: Idempotency keys on payments, webhooks and anything that gets retried.

items.name: SSRF
items.note: If you fetch user-supplied URLs (agents do), block internal addresses.

items.name: Production Incidents
items.note: Your first incident is the Phase 3 trigger — have a status page and a calm checklist.

items.name: Vertical Scaling
items.note: A bigger box is a legitimate first fix.

items.name: Latency
items.note: Measure before optimising — guessing is not profiling.

items.name: Throughput
items.note: The requests per second you can actually sustain — know your ceiling.

items.name: Metrics
items.note: Rate, errors and duration per endpoint.

items.name: Rate Limiting
items.note: Protect endpoints from abuse and runaway clients — auth endpoints first.

items.name: Long Polling
items.note: Often good enough before you reach for WebSockets.

items.name: Caching
items.note: Cache expensive reads once you've measured they're the bottleneck.

items.name: Horizontal Scaling
items.note: Stateless app servers so you can run more than one.

items.name: Load Balancing
items.note: Needed the moment you run two instances — often built into the platform.

items.name: Query Optimization
items.note: Read the EXPLAIN plan for your slowest queries.

items.name: Connection Pooling
items.note: Serverless + Postgres runs out of connections fast — use a pooler.

items.name: Message Queues
items.note: Move slow work (emails, AI jobs) off the request path.

items.name: Exponential Backoff
items.note: Back off with jitter so retries don't turn into a retry storm.

items.name: WebSockets
items.note: Two-way real-time; plan for reconnects and long-lived connections.

items.name: Eventual Consistency
items.note: Caches, replicas and queues mean reads can be stale — design for it.

items.name: Optimistic Locking
items.note: A version column stops two editors overwriting each other.

items.name: Memory Leaks
items.note: Memory that climbs until restart — watch long-running processes.

items.name: P99 Latency
items.note: Averages lie — the slowest 1% is someone's whole experience.

items.name: Cold Starts
items.note: The serverless first-request delay; keep functions lean or warm.

items.name: Cost Optimization
items.note: Read the cloud bill monthly and set budget alerts.

items.name: Rolling Deployments
items.note: Replace instances gradually — most platforms do this by default.

items.name: API Versioning
items.note: Version once someone else's code depends on your API.

items.name: Build Caching
items.note: Fast CI matters once a second engineer is waiting on it.

items.name: Observability
items.note: Logs, metrics and traces connected, so you can answer questions you didn't plan for.

items.name: On-Call
items.note: Who gets paged, and with which runbook.

items.name: Postmortems
items.note: A blameless write-up after every real incident.

items.name: Cache Invalidation
items.note: Decide how stale is acceptable before you cache anything.

items.name: Circuit Breakers
items.note: Stop calling a dependency that's already failing.

items.name: Dead Letter Queues
items.note: Failed messages park somewhere visible instead of vanishing.

items.name: Pub/Sub
items.note: One event, many consumers.

items.name: Distributed Locks
items.note: Stop two instances running the same job.

items.name: Pessimistic Locking
items.note: Lock rows for balances and inventory (SELECT … FOR UPDATE).

items.name: Deadlocks
items.note: Consistent lock ordering and short transactions.

items.name: Thread Safety
items.note: Shared mutable state across threads or workers.

items.name: Schema Versioning
items.note: Expand-and-contract migrations while users are live.

items.name: JWT Rotation
items.note: Short-lived tokens, a refresh flow, key rotation and revocation.

items.name: HTTP/2 & HTTP/3
items.note: Mostly handled by your CDN or host — know what you're getting.

items.name: Autoscaling
items.note: Scale on real signals, with a ceiling so a bug can't scale your bill.

items.name: Read Replicas
items.note: Offload reads and accept replica lag.

items.name: Replication
items.note: High availability for the database.

items.name: Disaster Recovery
items.note: A written recovery target and a rehearsed recovery.

items.name: Failover
items.note: Automatic switch to a standby when the primary dies.

items.name: SLIs
items.note: The few numbers that define "working" for users.

items.name: SLOs
items.note: Targets on those numbers — reliability as a product decision.

items.name: Infrastructure as Code
items.note: Environments rebuilt from code, not console clicks.

items.name: Terraform
items.note: The most common infrastructure-as-code tool.

items.name: Blue-Green Deployment
items.note: Two environments and an instant switch — double cost while it runs.

items.name: Liveness & Readiness Probes
items.note: The orchestrator restarts dead apps and holds traffic until they're ready.

items.name: API Gateways
items.note: One front door for auth, rate limits and routing across services.

items.name: CAP Theorem
items.note: During a network split, you choose consistency or availability.

items.name: gRPC
items.note: Typed, fast service-to-service calls.

items.name: Distributed Tracing
items.note: Follow one request across services.

items.name: Error Budgets
items.note: Spend unreliability deliberately on shipping speed.

items.name: Kubernetes
items.note: When you truly run many services — a budget decision, not a default.

items.name: Helm Charts
items.note: Packaging for Kubernetes deployments.

items.name: Service Discovery
items.note: Services find each other without hard-coded addresses.

items.name: Canary Releases
items.note: Release to 1% first, watch, then widen.

items.name: Event-Driven Architecture
items.note: Services react to events instead of calling each other.

items.name: Distributed Transactions
items.note: Avoid them when you can.

items.name: Saga Pattern
items.note: Multi-step workflows with compensating actions.

items.name: Backpressure
items.note: Slow the producer when consumers can't keep up.

items.name: Partitioning
items.note: Split big tables, often by time.

items.name: Leader Election
items.note: Exactly one node in charge.

items.name: Network Partitions
items.note: Nodes that can't see each other — decide the behaviour in advance.

items.name: Clock Skew
items.note: Machine clocks disagree — never order events by wall clock alone.

items.name: Tail Latency
items.note: At fan-out scale, the slowest backend sets your speed.

items.name: Garbage Collection
items.note: GC pauses show up as latency spikes at scale.

items.name: Chaos Engineering
items.note: Break things on purpose to prove recovery works.

items.name: TCP vs UDP
items.note: Reliability versus speed — matters for real-time media and games.

items.name: SSO
items.note: SAML/OIDC login — enterprise buyers ask early in the sales cycle.

items.name: Audit Logs
items.note: Who did what, and when — a standard enterprise request.

items.name: SLAs
items.note: Contractual uptime — promise only what your SLOs support.

items.name: SOC2 & Audits
items.note: The security-questionnaire gate on B2B deals.

items.name: Data Residency
items.note: Customers require their data kept in their region.

items.name: Edge Caching
items.note: Cache dynamic content close to users.

items.name: WAF
items.note: Filter malicious traffic before it reaches the app.

items.name: DDoS Protection
items.note: Absorb floods — a CDN-level service.

items.name: GDPR & Privacy
items.note: Consent, export and deletion at consumer scale.

items.name: Accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA)
items.note: A legal requirement for many EU consumer services.

items.name: Sharding
items.note: Split data across databases — the last resort after replicas and caching.

items.name: Multi-Region Deployment
items.note: Serve users close to them and survive a region outage.

overrides.extra: Sign BAAs with vendors that touch the data — including your LLM provider.
P1 decision: never touch raw card data — let Stripe or Razorpay hold it.
Verifiable parental consent before a child's data goes in.
One unprotected endpoint calling a paid model can run up a bill overnight — rate limiting moves up from P3.
EAA has applied since 28 Jun 2025 (WCAG 2.1 AA via EN 301 549); micro-enterprises are exempt.
Consent notices, breach reporting and children's-data rules apply from 13 May 2027.
